newsitem.title: TURKMENISTAN: Turkmens deny Taleban arms cross their territory.
newsitem.headline: Turkmens deny Taleban arms cross their territory.

text.p: Turkmenistan on Wednesday described Russian media reports that arms were being transported across its territory to the Islamic Taleban militia in neighbouring Afghanistan as "disinformation".
"It is all disinformation and insinuations," said a statement from the former Soviet republic's foreign ministry, read out on state television.
"Turkmenistan is a neutral state and is against intervention in any armed conflict," the statement said.
On Monday, Radio Russia, monitored by the British Broadcasting Corporation (BBC), reported that arms were being funnelled to the Taleban through Turkmenistan, which borders Afghanistan.

Turkmenistan was the only country out of the five ex-Soviet Central Asian states not to attend a regional security meeting in Tajikistan on Saturday where a possible Taleban advance towards their borders was top of the agenda.
Central Asian leaders, most of them former Communist Party bosses, fear the Taleban's radical brand of Islam and want to stop Afghanistan's civil war from crossing their borders.

Turkmenistan, a largely desert nation of 3.8 million and rich in oil and gas, also plans to build a gas pipeline with U.S. oil major Unocal Corp from the republic through Afghan territory to Pakistan.
